paras: The Ste. Genevieve posse shooting occurred in September 1903, when Sheriff Berry of Ste. Genevieve County, Missouri, and a posse shot and wounded a Black man they took to be Robert Bishop, wanted for a shooting at Oakville. The local Fair Play later reported that the jailed man "proved to be the wrong man."

On Friday night, September 11, Bishop was accused of shooting Sam Ellis and a woman known as "Black Ida" at a railroad camp at Oakville, St. Louis County. The foreman, Charles A. Waddell, blamed jealousy and said lynching threats drove Bishop to flee. The St. Louis Republic said other graders tried to hang him.
Constable John Schaper circulated his description, and Ste. Genevieve was warned to watch for him.

On Sunday morning, September 13, a man matching the description was seen at Burke's camp near Little Rock landing, and the sheriff raised a posse. In the Fair Play's account, the man ran for the woods when called on to surrender, and one of the posse shot him in the head and body. After an exchange of shots he escaped; he was captured the next day at St. Mary's and jailed.
Schaper and a Black man came on Thursday to identify the prisoner, who was not Bishop but stayed in jail for carrying concealed weapons.

Two Missouri white papers carried the shooting; no Black-press report appears in the coverage. The Republic, relying on word sent to the sheriff's office in Clayton, headlined "Negro Wounded by Posse" and "Sheriff Captures Robert Bishop After Desperate Fight." The Fair Play's local item also described a "desperate battle with a negro" and noted the mistaken identity without comment.

The Republic said the man opened fire with a revolver, was hit four times by buckshot, "seriously" wounded, and taken to a hospital, and dated the capture to September 16. The Fair Play, local and alone in reporting the identification, said the posse fired first and the wounds were not serious. The Fair Play also said "Black Ida" was killed; the Republic said only that she was shot.

reader.title: Ste. Genevieve posse shooting
bases: A sheriff-led posse shot and wounded a Black man while trying to arrest a fugitive (A2, A3).
The Republic (A2) and the local Fair Play (A3) separately report the posse shooting and capture, though they differ on details.

accounts.label: Sheriff's office in Clayton (St. Louis Republic)
accounts.gist: Bishop was found in bushes outside the town, drew a .41 revolver and opened fire when called on to surrender; the posse returned fire with buckshot, hit him four times and took him to a hospital.

accounts.label: Local paper (Ste. Genevieve Fair Play)
accounts.gist: A man answering the description ran for the woods when told to surrender and was shot by a posse member in the head and body; after exchanging shots he escaped, was captured next day, and proved not to be Bishop.

accounts.label: Camp foreman Waddell
accounts.gist: Bishop shot Ellis and 'Black Ida' out of jealousy and fled to St. Louis, frightened by threats of lynching.

framing.detail: The Republic headlined 'Negro Wounded by Posse' and 'Sheriff Captures Robert Bishop After Desperate Fight', treating the wounded man as Bishop and the shooting as a response to his fire.
The Fair Play's unheaded local item called it a 'desperate battle with a negro' and noted without comment that the prisoner was the wrong man and was kept in jail on a weapons charge.
